/didyouknow: Play Did You Know. You and your group share ideas without names, see who brought each one at the end, and each keep the list.

For: You lead a meeting, a class or a team and want everyone to share something new. You were sent a link to a game someone else leads: read You need and Words used here, then start at Everyone else joins.

You need: A regular browser window on every device, not a Private, Incognito or InPrivate one. On an iPhone or iPad, iOS 18.4 or newer. A room name and a secret, one word each, which the host makes up. For the host, a chat or email app to send a link.

Words used here: The command line is the box along the top of the app. The room bar is the small strip just under it that shows who is in the room. The notes desk is the panel where ideas are written and read. A tile is one hexagon on the screen, and a page is the screen of tiles you are looking at. Every word you type starts with a /, as in “/join”: click the command line, type it and press **Enter**. The / turns into the command icon as you type it, which is right. Click the command line again whenever the notes desk has opened, because the desk takes the cursor, and anything typed there becomes an idea, even “/reveal”. Without a /, the line makes a tile that everyone in the room sees. A part in italics, like <your idea>, is yours to change, and you leave out the angle brackets. A message from the app fades after a few seconds.

On a phone: Press **add** at the foot of the app, type the word in the “name it…” box and press **Add**. The box stays open, so press **add** again to put it away and see the message. To bring the command line back, hold an empty spot on the page.
Part: The host sets up the room

Step 1 -- Open hypercomb.io, and press **Start** if the app says “Welcome to Hypercomb”. The app installs itself and reloads the page. If a card says “Make this hive yours.”, press **Start empty**. Done when the command line along the top says “share intent...”.

Step 2 -- Type “/join <room name> <secret> hypercomb.com” and press **Enter**, with one word each for the room name and the secret, which is a password you make up. The app opens a room that anyone who types the same three words can join, so make both words hard to guess. The last word, hypercomb.com, is an open meeting point meant for trying things out. Done when the room bar says “Live” and “you're the first one here”. If it says “<number> in the room” instead, someone is already there: type the line again with a new room name and secret.

Step 3 -- Type “/start did you know” and press **Enter** on the page you want to play on. Stay on the screen you see, or left-click a tile to walk into its page first. The app makes a tile there named for the page, “did-you-know” at the top and “did-you-know-lecture” inside a page called lecture, and opens the notes desk on it. Start the game after you join, because a game started before you join stays on your device. Done when the notes desk is open with a title that starts “did-you-know”.

Step 4 -- Press **Invite** in the room bar, and send the link and the address of this page, didyouknow.hypercomb.com, to everyone who is playing. The app copies the link or opens your device’s share sheet: pick an app there, because closing the sheet sends nothing. The link carries the secret, so send it only to the people playing. Done when the app says “Meeting link copied”, or “Meeting link shared” after you picked an app, and the room bar counts people as they join. If the app shows the link with a **Share** button instead, press that button.
Callout: Once someone has joined, **Invite** leaves the room bar, so to send the link again, type “/invite” with no tile selected.
Part: Everyone else joins

Step 1 -- Open the link you were sent, and press **Start** if the app says “Welcome to Hypercomb”. The app installs itself and reloads the page. If a card says “Make this hive yours.”, press **Start empty**. If the card has no **Start** button, press **Copy meeting link** and paste it into the address bar of your own browser, not a Private window. Done when a sheet titled “Join the room” asks you to join.

Step 2 -- Press **Join** on the sheet. The app puts you in the room and walks you to the host’s page, and your command line goes back to making tiles, so type the / before each word. Done when the room bar says “Live” and counts you in, like “3 in the room (3 here)”, and a tile whose name starts “did-you-know” shows on the page. On a narrow phone, tap the count beside the dot to read the bar.
Part: Playing
Callout: The app hides names on the screen, but the data the room shares still holds them, and anyone can type “/reveal”, so play with people you trust.

Step 1 -- Give yourself a name: press the **+** badge in the room bar, type your name and press **Enter**. Without a name, the reveal shows you as eight letters and numbers. Done when the badge shows the first letters of your name instead of the **+**.

Step 2 -- Share something you think the others do not know: type “/did-you-know <your idea>” and press **Enter**, for example “/did-you-know octopuses have three hearts”. Your idea goes to the room with no name on it, and the notes desk opens. Stay on the host’s page and do not click the did-you-know tile, because that walks you into it; if you did, right-click, or press **back** on a phone. Done when your idea is a line in the notes desk.

Step 3 -- Read the others in the notes desk. If the desk is closed, press the sticky-note button beside the command line, named **writing**, and choose the did-you-know tile in its list. Done when the foot of the desk counts the room once someone else is in it, like “3 here · 5 notes · 1 yours · 4 to take”.
Callout: If the app says “Did You Know is off here”, stay on the host’s page, wait until its did-you-know tile shows, and type your idea again, and do not type “/did-you-know on”.
Part: Ending the game
Callout: Stay in the room with this window open until everyone has typed “/collect”, because an idea leaves with the person who wrote it.

Step 1 -- If you are the host, go to the page where you started the game, type “/reveal” and press **Enter** when everyone has shared. A game reveals only once, so do not reveal early. The app writes one note on the tile, starting “Revealed ·”, that lists each idea the host’s window has seen with the name of the person who brought it. Every desk shows each name at the end of the line, but your own ideas show no name on your own desk, so look in that note. Everyone else waits for the note. Done when the app says “revealed <number> ideas from <number> people — the names are on the tile for everyone”.

Step 2 -- Keep the ideas: type “/collect” and press **Enter**. The app takes every idea you can see onto your own did-you-know tile for this page, and leaves the reveal note where it is. If it says some ideas are still arriving, type it again. Done when the app says “collected <number> ideas onto this page’s did-you-know tile”, or “nothing new to collect” when you already hold them all.
Callout: Do not press a name, the ✕ beside an idea, or **Hide the room** on the desk, because that hides ideas from you and “/collect” skips them.
What it costs: Nothing.

When you are done: You have a list of ideas on your own did-you-know tile for that page, and it stays after the room is gone. To read it later, go to the page where you played, press the **writing** button, and choose the did-you-know tile in the desk’s list of tiles. On a phone, hold an empty spot on the page first. Each page keeps its own game and its own list, and a page’s game is played once for now: the ideas and the reveal stay on its tile.
